paragraphs.source_en: Though the Ōshū affair infuriated Hideyoshi, he had no choice but to act as Rikyū had advised. After sending Hashiba Hidetsugu and Tokugawa Ieyasu to urge Date Masamune to come to the capital, he went personally to Kiyosu Castle, rebuked Masamune there, and returned to Kyoto on the third day of the second month. Throughout this time, Hideyoshi had not forgotten the matter of Rikyū; it remained lodged in his throat like a fishbone. As time passed, that hatred gradually became warped.

units.source_en: After sending Hashiba Hidetsugu and Tokugawa Ieyasu to urge Date Masamune to come to the capital, he went personally to Kiyosu Castle, rebuked Masamune there, and returned to Kyoto on the third day of the second month.

units.source_en: Throughout this time, Hideyoshi had not forgotten the matter of Rikyū; it remained lodged in his throat like a fishbone.
units.source_zh: 在这期间，秀吉并没有忘掉利休的事，如鲠在喉。

units.source_en: As time passed, that hatred gradually became warped.

paragraphs.source_zh: 秀吉为奥州的事恼火，却只有照利休所言去做，别无他法。派羽柴秀次和德川家康去催伊达政宗进京后，他亲自前往清洲城，在那里斥责政宗，又于二月初三返京。在这期间，秀吉并没有忘掉利休的事，如鲠在喉。这种憎恶已随着时间的流逝逐渐扭曲。

paragraphs.source_en: A man like Hideyoshi could never endure the thought that he and Rikyū stood opposed; he had to find some subtle way of delivering the other man a stunning blow. By then, this “hatred” lay concealed within the Kampaku’s heart.

He merely wished to shock and subdue the man who was gradually setting himself against him.
